This study estimated genetic parameters, inbreeding coefficients and effective population size and evaluated the effect of inbreeding on morphometric and performance traits in Mangalarga Marchador horses. Genealogical, morphological, and performance data from 48,075 "batida" gait horses registered by ABCCMM between 1950 and 2018 were used. Heritability and generation interval were estimated, along with inbreeding coefficients derived from the complete pedigree (N=222,990). The effect of inbreeding was estimated as the regression of each trait on the individual inbreeding coefficient (F), fitted as a covariate in single-trait animal models. Heritability ranged from 0.23±0.009 to 0.49±0.004. Mean inbreeding in the whole pedigree was 0.013±0.035. A total of 81,593 animals (36.6%) were inbred (F > 0); among these inbred animals, F ranged from 0.001 to 0.438, with a mean of 0.035±0.051, and 62,755 (76.9%) were females and 18,838 (23.1%) males. The generation interval was 9.1 years, and the effective population size was 26.61. Inbreeding was significantly associated with ten of the twelve morphometric traits. Regression coefficients (β, in cm per unit of F, i.e., from F = 0 to F = 1) were -3.71, -3.80, -2.28, -1.31, -1.68, -1.68, -4.30, -1.29, -1.45, and -4.12 for withers height, croup height, neck length, back and loin length, croup length, shoulder length, body length, head width, croup width, and thoracic perimeter, respectively, corresponding to reductions of 0.13 to 0.43 cm per 10% increase in F. The estimates for head length (-0.30) and cannon bone perimeter (-0.04) did not differ significantly from zero. Morphofunctional score decreased by 2.19 points per unit of F (0.22 points per 10% increase in F), whereas the estimates for gait (1.73) and total (-0.49) scores did not differ from zero. Increasing inbreeding was associated with small reductions in body measurements and morphofunctional scores, whereas no significant association was found for the gait score. Although these effects are of small magnitude at the current levels of inbreeding, the decline in effective population size in recent generations indicates that mating strategies to control the increase in inbreeding should be adopted.

title: Multi-omics analysis uncovers enhanced toxicity associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and redox imbalance following co-exposure to tris(2-chloroisopropyl) phosphate and polystyrene nanoplastics in Caenorhabditis elegans.
abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) have emerged as important vectors for persistent organic pollutants, raising concerns about their potential physiological and ecological risks to living organisms across biological systems. Through a Trojan horse-like mechanism, NPs can enhance the bioavailability and toxicity of co-occurring contaminants or even induce novel toxic responses. Consequently, co-exposure scenarios may induce enhanced toxicity relative to single exposures, emphasizing the need for mechanistic investigations at the molecular-systems level. Nevertheless, the roles of NPs and the molecular mechanisms governing their synergistic interactions with other pollutants remain poorly understood in terrestrial species. In this study, we investigated the toxic effects of co-exposure to polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs, <50 nm) and tris(2-chloroisopropyl) phosphate (TCPP) in Caenorhabditis elegans. The results demonstrated that co-exposure markedly exacerbated toxicity compared to single exposures, as evidenced by decreased survival, mitochondrial dysfunction, and increased oxidative stress. Multi-omics analyses revealed coordinated metabolic and transcriptional perturbations associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and a redox imbalance. Metabolomic profiling indicated dysregulation of pathways related to mitochondrial energy metabolism, including the tricarboxylic acid cycle and cysteine and methionine metabolism, whereas glutathione metabolism was specifically enriched under co-exposure conditions. Transcriptomic analysis further identified significant alterations in proteostasis and cellular stress responses, including ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, the proteasome system, autophagy, and RNA degradation. These findings were further validated in Caco-2 cells, where co-exposure significantly exacerbated cytotoxicity, along with mitochondrial dysfunction and increased oxidative stress. Collectively, our results suggest that co-exposure to PS-NPs and TCPP disrupts mitochondrial homeostasis and redox balance, which are associated with enhanced toxicity under co-exposure conditions.

title: Conjugation of Nosiheptide to a Bidentate Catechol to Overcome Permeability Limitations in a Gram-Negative Model Strain.
abstract: Antibiotic penetration to intracellular targets is severely restricted by the outer membrane barrier of Gram-negative bacteria. Nosiheptide (NOS, 16) is potent against Gram-positive bacteria but ineffective against the tested Gram-negative model strain because its large molecular size limits efficient membrane penetration. Siderophore conjugation provides a "Trojan horse" strategy that exploits bacterial iron uptake pathways to overcome this permeability barrier. Bidentate catechol siderophore mimetics (15a-15d) were synthesized and used to construct a siderophore-NOS conjugate (17). The antibacterial activity of conjugate 17 was evaluated against Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1. The role of siderophore-mediated uptake was investigated by comparing antibacterial activity under iron-depleted and iron-rich conditions, alongside a transporter-deficient mutant strain. Molecular docking was performed to compare the interactions of conjugate 17 and nosiheptide with the ribosomal target, and confocal fluorescence imaging of Escherichia coli was conducted to assess cellular uptake. Conjugate 17 exhibited antibacterial activity against P. aeruginosa PAO1, particularly under iron-limited conditions. The reduced antibacterial activity under iron-rich conditions suggests that bacterial pathways involved in iron acquisition may contribute to the uptake of conjugate 17. Molecular docking analysis predicted a potentially favorable binding mode for conjugate 17 within the ribosomal target site; meanwhile, confocal fluorescence imaging revealed greater cellular accumulation of conjugate 17 than that of nosiheptide in E. coli. The siderophore-NOS conjugation strategy enabled the macromolecular thiopeptide antibiotic nosiheptide to overcome the intrinsic permeability barrier in the tested Gram-negative model strain through bacterial iron transport pathways. These findings provide a foundation for further evaluation of this strategy against a broader range of Gram-negative pathogens.

title: Defining the Diphyllin Pharmacophore for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral V-ATPase Inhibition by Structure-Guided Scaffold Modifications.
abstract: The threat of emerging viral diseases presents a critical societal need for broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. A key contribution to antiviral options would be a broad-spectrum agent that can treat a wide variety of viral diseases. Vacuolar H-ATPase (V-ATPase), a host proton pump critical for endosomal acidification, serves an essential role in facilitating the entry of multiple viruses. Diphyllin, a naturally occurring V-ATPase inhibitor, displays potent antiviral activity but is limited by suboptimal drug-like properties, including selectivity and metabolic instability. Molecular modeling enabled the identification of a conserved binding site on the V-ATPase a-subunit consisting of three distinct sub-pockets. Docking analyses of ninety-five known diphyllin derivatives demonstrated that active analogs effectively occupy all three subpockets, informing a structure-based design approach. A library of novel diphyllin analogs with modifications to a single-ring system showed 50-fold increases in potency for antiviral activity against Ebola, Venezuelan equine encephalitis, and Chikungunya viruses and exhibiting improvements in metabolic stability and permeability.

title: Cross-species horse-to-dog fecal microbiota transplantation as a novel nature-inspired therapy for non-responsive chronic enteropathy in dogs.
abstract: Canine chronic enteropathy (CE) is frequently associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has emerged as a potential microbiota-modulating therapeutic approach. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes and gut microbiota effects of a novel cross-species horse-to-dog FMT in 20 dogs with CE. Clinical response was assessed using the Canine Chronic Enteropathy Clinical Activity Index (CCECAI) at 30 days and approximately 1 year after treatment. Gut microbiota composition was characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and compared with healthy reference dogs and the equine donor. At baseline, dogs with CE displayed reduced microbial diversity, marked compositional differences from healthy dogs, depletion of health-associated taxa, including members of Oscillospirales, Limosilactobacillus, Collinsella, and the Peptoclostridium complex, and enrichment of Escherichia-Shigella. Following FMT, 13/20 dogs (65%) showed a positive clinical response at 30 days and 16/20 (80%) were classified as long-term responders, with 13/20 (65%) achieving clinical remission at 1 year. At 30 days, no significant global changes in alpha or beta diversity were detected; however, ordination suggested a shift of post-FMT profiles toward the healthy reference configuration, accompanied by taxonomic changes consistent with partial microbiota restoration, including an increased relative abundance of Peptoclostridium-associated ASVs, including those putatively assigned to Peptoacetobacter hiranonis, and trends toward enrichment of Holdemanella and Turicibacter. ASV-sharing analysis revealed minimal persistence of horse-derived microorganisms in recipient dogs. A multilayer predictive analysis identified baseline Holdemanella and Parabacteroides as candidate markers of favorable clinical response, whereas Clostridium, Corynebacterium, Enterococcus, and Romboutsia were associated with poorer outcomes. These findings support further evaluation of cross-species horse-to-dog FMT as a therapeutic strategy for canine CE and suggest a predominantly biostimulatory mechanism acting on the resident gut microbiota.

title: Digital preservation of multispecies heart morphology using smartphone LiDAR-assisted photogrammetry.
abstract: Fresh biological specimens represent the most realistic material for anatomical study. However, fresh organs are difficult to digitize due to their deformability, moist reflective surfaces, and rapid post-mortem deterioration. These limitations are particularly relevant for the heart, an anatomically complex organ whose three-dimensional (3D) architecture and species-specific variations are challenging to document and preserve. This study developed and evaluated a complete workflow for the digital preservation of fresh comparative cardiac anatomy by combining smartphone LiDAR-assisted photogrammetry with a cloud-based platform for interactive 3D and augmented reality (AR) visualization. One fresh heart from each of five animal species (dog, sheep, pig, cow, and horse) was digitized using a standardized acquisition protocol to explore the applicability of the workflow across specimens with different sizes and morphological characteristics. Quantitative assessment of three selected external linear dimensions was performed through direct comparison between physical specimens and their digital reconstructions, while anatomical evaluation was conducted by experienced veterinary anatomists. The reconstructed models were subsequently integrated into a cloud-based platform for Web3D and AR visualization. Across 15 paired morphometric comparisons, the mean absolute percentage error was 4.08% (range: 0.83-8.28%), indicating close agreement for the external linear dimensions evaluated. Independent expert evaluation using a structured assessment rubric confirmed preservation of species-specific morphological characteristics, major cardiac landmarks, and external anatomical relationships across all models. In addition to complete heart reconstructions, the workflow was successfully applied to a dissected heart specimen, providing a proof of concept for the digital preservation and visualization of selected intracardiac structures. Following integration into the cloud platform, the models were made accessible through interactive Web3D and AR environments with anatomical labelling and cross-device compatibility. Beyond its potential educational applications in veterinary anatomy, the proposed workflow integrates acquisition, assessment, and cloud-based dissemination within a single digital pipeline, providing a practical framework for digital anatomical collections representing different mammalian cardiac morphologies, future anatomical repositories, and the long-term preservation and dissemination of fresh comparative cardiac anatomy.

title: Cranial Nerve Passageways of the African (Loxodonta africana) and Asian (Elephas maximus) Elephant in Comparison to the Dog, Horse, Cow and Pig.
abstract: This study provides a detailed, comparative anatomical analysis of the cranial nerve passageways in African (Loxodonta africana) and Asian (Elephas maximus) elephants, addressing a gap left by sparse historical literature. Using a combination of macroscopic photography and high-resolution, 128-slice helical computed tomography (CT) scans of adult and juvenile specimens, we mapped the internal anatomy of the floor of the cranium. Following the nomenclature of the Nomina Anatomica Veterinaria (NAV), we compared these findings with standard domestic veterinary models, including the dog, horse, cow and pig. Our comparative analysis illustrates that elephants possess distinct orbital fissures and round foramina, rather than the combined foramen orbitorotundum typical of swine and ruminants and establishes that elephants possess distinct oval foramina and carotid canals, rather than the foramen lacerum typical of swine and equines. Most notably, we demonstrate a definitive alar canal perforating the pterygoid process, a feature shared with canines and equines but omitted in previous proboscidean literature. We resolve ambiguities in the literature by illustrating a short canal connecting the internal jugular foramen and the external tympanooccipital fissure, an anatomical feature shared with our standard veterinary models. Additionally, CT imaging confirmed that the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid bone accommodates a paranasal sinus that communicates with the sphenoid complex. By resolving historical ambiguities and providing the first photographically and CT-illustrated mapping of the cranial nerve pathways, this research establishes an updated, precise reference for elephant cranial anatomy and cranial nerve topography.

title: Seasonal welfare variation in outdoor group-housed horses: a two-year longitudinal study.
abstract: Outdoor group-housed horses are exposed to seasonal environmental variation, but longitudinal data on welfare-related indicators in these systems remain limited. This observational study described seasonal and interannual variation in welfare-related indicators in 80 horses kept at six Italian outdoor group-housing stables over two years. Across eight seasonal visits, animal- and resource-based indicators from an adapted Animal Welfare Indicators (AWIN)-based protocol were recorded; an exploratory cumulative animal-based measure score (cABM score) and first-year hair cortisol concentrations were also analyzed. Environmental conditions varied markedly across seasons and between years, particularly temperature, humidity, and precipitation. Abnormal breathing and coughing were rarely observed, while stereotypies and human-animal relationship responses showed little temporal variation; however, body condition, integumentary and hoof-related indicators, and water cleanliness identified welfare-relevant management priorities. The cABM score differed among seasons (P = 0.026) and showed a significant year × season interaction (P < 0.001), indicating seasonal and interannual variation in the cumulative number of altered animal-based indicators. Hair cortisol concentrations varied by season (P < 0.001), with seasonal patterns differing among stables (season × stable, P < 0.001). After adjustment for stable and the season × stable interaction, neither the association between cABM score and hair cortisol concentrations (P = 0.648) nor the season × cABM score interaction (P = 0.258) was statistically significant. None of the season-specific slopes differed significantly from zero. Hair cortisol was therefore interpreted as a contextual physiological marker of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity rather than a direct indicator of welfare state. Overall, welfare-related indicators in outdoor group-housed horses varied across seasons and years. Repeated multidimensional monitoring may help identify periods and indicators requiring targeted management attention in year-round outdoor systems.

title: Ferritin Heavy Chain 1 (FTH-1) Overexpression Is Associated with HIF-1α Expression in Equine Sarcoids.
abstract: Equine sarcoid is the most common cutaneous neoplasm in horses and is strongly associated with bovine papillomavirus (BPV) infection. Ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH-1), a key regulator of cellular iron homeostasis, has been implicated in tumour biology and hypoxic responses. Given the previously reported expression of hypoxia-inducible factor 1 alpha (HIF-1α) in equine sarcoids, this study investigated FTH-1 expression and its relationship with HIF-1α. Immunohistochemistry for FTH-1 was performed on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues from 35 BPV-positive equine sarcoids and 10 normal skin samples. Staining was evaluated according to intensity and percentage of positive cells. Normal skin showed weak FTH-1 immunoreactivity, mainly limited to the basal epidermal layer skin adnexa and normal fibroblasts, whereas all sarcoids exhibited cytoplasmic immunolabelling in neoplastic fibroblasts. Strong FTH-1 immunoreactivity (score 3) was observed in 30/35 cases (85.7%), while the remaining 5/35 cases (14.3%) showed moderate staining (score 2). The percentage of FTH-1-positive cells was significantly higher in sarcoids than in normal skin (Mann-Whitney U test, p < 0.0001). A strong positive correlation was found between FTH-1 and HIF-1α immunopositive cell percentages (r = 0.942, p = 3.24 × 10-17). These findings demonstrate increased FTH-1 expression in equine sarcoids and a significant association with HIF-1α expression, suggesting a possible involvement of iron metabolism in sarcoid biology.

title: Isolation, Multidrug Resistance Profiling, and Whole-Genome Analysis of Escherichia coli from Foals with Diarrhea in Ili, Xinjiang, China.
abstract: Escherichia coli (E. coli) is a leading cause of diarrhea in neonatal foals, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains poses a growing threat to equine health and public health. However, antimicrobial resistance surveillance in equine E. coli remains limited, particularly in Xinjiang, a major horse-breeding region in China. To isolate and identify E. coli from diarrheic foals in Ili, Xinjiang, characterize their antimicrobial resistance phenotypes, and perform whole-genome sequencing on a representative MDR strain to elucidate its resistance mechanisms, virulence potential, and transmission risk. A total of 78 fecal samples were collected from diarrheic foals between May 2025 and June 2026. Isolates were identified by culture, Gram staining, and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The antibiotic susceptibility of the isolated bacteria was determined using the Kirby-Bauer diffusion method. A representative MDR strain, YN1, was subjected to PacBio and Illumina whole-genome sequencing. Resistance genes, virulence factors, and mobile genetic elements were annotated using CARD, VFDB, and CAZy databases, and key findings were validated by PCR, biofilm assays, and a murine pathogenicity model. A total of 58 E. coli strains were isolated (isolation rate, 74.36%), with the highest rate (83.33%) in foals aged 0-3 months. MDR was detected in 63.79% of isolates. Strain YN1 possessed a 4,951,512 bp chromosome and a 130,938 bp plasmid (cgMLST type cgST134023), encoding 107 predicted resistance genes and 204 predicted virulence determinants. Resistance was mediated primarily by chromosomally encoded efflux systems, supplemented by the plasmid-borne blaTEM. YN1 formed strong biofilms and caused lethal infection in mice within an average of 16 h, with severe hemorrhage and congestion in the lungs, spleen, and liver. MDR E. coli is highly prevalent among diarrheic foals in Ili, Xinjiang. The representative strain YN1 carried extensive resistance and virulence determinants and exhibited strong pathogenicity, highlighting the need for strengthened antimicrobial resistance surveillance and rational antimicrobial use in equine practice.

title: Veterinary Vaccine Adjuvants: Past, Present, and Future.
abstract: Vaccine adjuvants enhance immune responses and improve the effectiveness of veterinary vaccines. However, their performance and safety vary across animal species, vaccine formulations, and production systems. This narrative review examines the historical development, mechanisms, applications, safety, and regulatory considerations of major veterinary adjuvant classes. Aluminum salts are widely used because of their affordability and ability to enhance antibody responses, although their effects on cellular immunity may be limited. Oil-based emulsions can provide strong and durable immune responses, particularly in inactivated vaccines for livestock and poultry, but injection-site reactions and formulation stability remain important concerns. Saponin-based systems can stimulate both antibody and cellular immunity, with applications in equine and canine vaccines. Polymeric nanoparticles and pattern-recognition receptor agonists offer promising approaches for mucosal vaccination and targeted immune activation, although further validation in veterinary species is needed. Adjuvant selection must consider antigen properties, species-specific immune responses, age, administration route, protective efficacy, manufacturing feasibility, and regulatory requirements. Future research should prioritize comparative studies in target species, predictive biomarkers, improved vaccine stability, and evaluation of complete antigen-adjuvant formulations. These considerations may support the development of safer, more effective, and practical veterinary vaccines.

title: From the Conglutinating Complex Fixation Test to the Saiduldin Test: Development, Veterinary Evidence Base, and Prospects for Contemporary Validation.
abstract: The Saiduldin Test (ST), originally developed as the Conglutinating Complex Fixation Test (CCFT), is a complement-dependent serological method based on specific antigen-antibody interaction followed by conglutinin-mediated secondary aggregation. This review aimed to systematize and critically evaluate the scientific evidence concerning the immunological foundations, historical development, standardization, and veterinary diagnostic applications of ST, with particular emphasis on bovine and ovine brucellosis, while also considering its applications to other infectious diseases and identifying priorities for contemporary validation. Scientific publications, dissertations, field-trial reports, patents, methodological instructions, and regulatory and technical documents reflecting the successive development of the method were analyzed. The most extensive evidence base concerns bovine brucellosis and includes large-scale field trials, comparisons with established serological methods, and longitudinal observations of animals with discordant test results. ST was subsequently adapted for other infections and animal species, including ovine brucellosis, bovine leukemia, camel surra, equine dourine, and ovine chlamydiosis. The conglutinin-dependent principle was applied both to the detection of specific antibodies and to the identification of circulating immune complexes. Historical investigations demonstrate the practical applicability and feasibility of standardizing ST and, in certain populations, higher serological detection rates than those obtained with some comparator tests. However, the absence of independent confirmation of infection status in most early studies and limitations of their designs prevent higher positivity rates from being interpreted as evidence of superior diagnostic sensitivity or specificity. Contemporary evaluation should therefore follow a predefined intended diagnostic purpose and include reagent standardization, assessment of analytical characteristics, diagnostic cut-off, sensitivity, specificity, repeatability, and interlaboratory reproducibility, together with prospective investigation of discordant results and seroconversion dynamics. The antibody-detection format of ST for bovine brucellosis represents the most appropriate initial model for validation. Stepwise independent validation would allow the diagnostic value of ST and its potential role in contemporary veterinary diagnostics to be determined objectively.

title: From the Wild to the Uniform: Clinical and Echocardiographic Monitoring of Young Murgese Horses During the First Year of Training.
abstract: Excessive training load can lead to maladaptation with measurable imbalances at the cardiovascular, endocrine, and hematological levels. The first aim of this study was to evaluate conventional and advanced echocardiographic parameters in young Murgese horses during training over one year, in order to assess the effect of training on cardiac dimensions and function. The second aim was to assess the general conditions and to monitor work adaptation indices through clinical examinations and hematobiochemical tests. Young Murgese horses intended for training and working in the Carabinieri Army Forces were evaluated at four different training stages: at the stabling phase-enrolling (T0); at the end of the desensitization and ground-work phase, shortly before being ridden (T1); in the midst of ridden athletic preparation (T2); and at the end of the training period (T3-one year of training). Clinical, echocardiographic and haemato-biochemical exams were performed; data were analyzed over time by Friedman and Wilcoxon test. Bonferroni corrections were applied. A significant increase in ejection fraction (EF%) and shortening fraction (FS%) was documented between T0 and T1 (p = 0.016, p = 0.011, respectively). Moreover, left atrial dimensions increased between T0 and T2 (p = 0.021) and between T1 and T2 (p = 0.028). No additional statistically significant changes were observed for other echocardiographic parameters. Regarding clinical and laboratory variables, significant differences were noted for HCT, Hgb, RBC, WBC, lymphocytes, AST, urea, and lactate (p < 0.05). Our echocardiographic and hematobiochemical findings suggest that, in Murgese horses, training may have an impact on the cardiovascular system and on the metabolic axis during the athletic preparation phase. Maturation and other time-dependent factors could not be excluded as co-factors of the observed longitudinal changes.

title: Management Practices and Behaviour of Mares Throughout the Equine Chorionic Gonadotropin (eCG) Production Cycle in a Sample of Icelandic Farms: A Video-Based Assessment of Publicly Available Footage.
abstract: Welfare implications of repeated blood collection from pregnant mares for equine chorionic gonadotropin (eCG) production remain debated. This study aimed to describe mare-management practices in a sample of Icelandic farms, investigating behavioural responses to blood collection and associated management conditions using publicly available video footage. The analysis was performed while the mares were kept on pasture, as well as during the pre-collection waiting period and blood collection. A Fear, Anxiety and Stress (FAS) score (from 0 = relaxed to 5 = severe signs of FAS with aggression) was also assigned to each blood collection phase. Although limited, pasture observations highlighted generally good physical condition of mares and foals, with normal social behaviour. Mares waited an average of 1 h 40 min before blood collection, and greater pen crowding was associated with increased negative interactions among mares (p = 0.031). The blood collection procedure lasted about 8 min on average (range: 5.2-15.4 min). Most mares exhibited moderate to severe FAS during blood collection, with a significant effect of the phase (LRT p < 0.001). Blood draw was the phase with the highest likelihood of showing higher FAS scores in comparison with waiting time (OR = 9.91, 95% CI: 4.08-20.5). A significant increase in a depressed-like, non-responsive demeanour was recorded during more invasive handling phases (all p < 0.05). Even if our findings are limited by the nature of the analysed videos, this study identifies potential welfare concerns, including restrictive head positioning, incomplete post-venipuncture care, and continuation of procedures despite severe behavioural signs of stress.

title: Isolation and In Vitro Evaluation of Yeasts from Mare's Milk and Fermented Mare's Milk for Probiotic Potential.
abstract: Mare's milk and fermented mare's milk are potential sources of yeasts for probiotic screening. This study evaluated the in vitro probiotic potential of 23 yeast isolates from these sources. MALDI-TOF MS preliminarily identified 15 isolates as Kluyveromyces marxianus, four as Pichia manshurica, two as Pichia fermentans, one as Saccharomyces cerevisiae and one as Yarrowia lipolytica. Stress tolerance, solvent affinity, autoaggregation, coaggregation, hemolytic activity, and cell-free supernatant-mediated antibacterial activity were assessed. Relative viable counts, calculated against corresponding controls at the same 4-h endpoint, averaged below 6% under 0.3% bile salt exposure and below 1% at pH 2. Responses at pH 3 and elevated temperatures were variable. Solvent affinity ranged from 2.50% to 95.07%, with differences among isolates within each solvent (all p < 0.001). Autoaggregation ranged from 7.50% to 95.40% after 4 h. Coaggregation reached approximately 55% with Escherichia coli, 49% with Salmonella Enteritidis, and 50% with Staphylococcus aureus. Supernatants from 10 isolates inhibited at least one indicator bacterium, and six inhibited all three. R3-4 produced the numerically largest mean inhibition zone against S. aureus (19.3 ± 1.2 mm). No detectable hemolysis was observed. An exploratory five-domain score highlighted R3-4 (putative Y. lipolytica) and four putative K. marxianus isolates, without indicating superiority across all traits. These phenotypic profiles inform further screening, molecular confirmation, comprehensive safety assessment, and equine-relevant functional validation remain necessary.

title: Modeling Venezuelan Equine Encephalitis Virus Infection of the Liver and Evaluation of a Host-Directed Therapeutic in an Organ-on-a-Chip Platform.
abstract: Early stages of host-virus interactions in peripheral tissues, such as the liver, are critical yet understudied determinants of alphavirus pathogenesis. We utilized a liver organ-on-a-chip (OOC) model consisting of primary human hepatocytes (PHHs) and Kupffer cells (KCs) to enable time-resolved tracking of Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus vaccine strain TC-83 (VEEV TC-83) replication kinetics, tissue damage, and host immunopathology. This platform was employed to evaluate the host-directed therapeutic Omaveloxolone (OMA), a known nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) activator. Productive VEEV infection induced acute liver injury, indicated by parallel increases in supernatant alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), alongside the newly identified pathogen-associated biomarkers γ-enolase (ENO2) and complement factor H-related protein 3 (CFHR3). Post-infection treatment with OMA within a nontoxic range altered inflammatory responses and modestly reduced viral load during the early stages, although this inhibitory efficacy was lost at later time points. Collectively, this OOC model enables the investigation of organ-specific events, demonstrating that peripheral liver responses to VEEV involve coordinated inflammatory and proteomic alterations that culminate in acute liver injury, potentially contributing to systemic inflammation and overall alphavirus disease severity.

title: From Systemic Infection to Central Nervous System Pathology: Virus-Induced Neuroinflammatory Cascades and Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption.
abstract: Viral infections are recognized triggers of neurological disease through immune-mediated mechanisms that induce acute and chronic neuroinflammation. Although the central nervous system (CNS) is protected by the blood-brain barrier (BBB), several pathogens can access the CNS through mechanisms including leukocyte-mediated "Trojan Horse" entry, endothelial transcytosis, and neuronal transport. Neuropathology frequently seems to be primarily caused by dysregulated host immune responses that activate glial cells and compromise the integrity of the blood-brain barrier. This mini-review summarizes current evidence linking BBB dysfunction to sustained neuroinflammatory cascades, emphasizing microglia-astrocyte interactions and downstream neuronal injury, including synaptic dysfunction and neurodegenerative changes. Using Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as representative examples, we discuss mechanisms of CNS entry, BBB disruption, microglial activation, astrocyte dysfunction, and excitotoxic neuronal injury. We further examine factors governing the transition from protective immune responses to persistent neuroinflammation, including viral latency, chronic immune activation, and microglial priming. Finally, we highlight recent advances in systems biology and systems bioinformatics that enable integration of multi-omics and network-level data to identify conserved pathways underlying virus-associated neurological disease and post-viral syndromes. BBB disruption represents a critical interface linking viral infection to CNS pathology. Convergent inflammatory mechanisms involving glial activation and impaired neurological and immune regulation contribute to persistent neurological dysfunction across diverse viral infections. Integrative systems-level approaches can assist in investigating these mechanisms, while they may also facilitate the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets capable of distinguishing resolving from persistent neuroinflammatory states.

title: Evidence of Natural Nervous Necrosis Virus Infection in Juvenile Greenfin Horse-Faced Filefish (Thamnaconus septentrionalis) During an Aquaculture Mortality Event.
abstract: Viral nervous necrosis (VNN), caused by nervous necrosis virus (NNV), is a devastating viral disease affecting marine fish aquaculture worldwide, particularly during larval and juvenile stages. Although NNV has a broad and expanding host range, the susceptibility of greenfin horse-faced filefish (Thamnaconus septentrionalis) has not been established. To determine whether T. septentrionalis is susceptible to NNV, we investigated an outbreak of abnormal mortality in juveniles from a marine aquaculture farm in Rizhao, Shandong Province, China. A comprehensive etiological investigation combined bacterial isolation and identification, real-time quantitative RT-PCR (RT-qPCR), tissue-distribution analysis, histopathology, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and RNA2-based phylogenetic analysis. Diseased fish exhibited characteristic VNN-like neurological signs, including spiral swimming, loss of equilibrium, anorexia, and body darkening. Several bacterial taxa, including Vibrio- and Tenacibaculum-related isolates, were recovered from diseased fish, indicating the possibility of bacterial involvement. However, the concurrent detection of abundant NNV RNA in neural tissues, together with characteristic neurological signs, compatible histopathological lesions, and NNV-like particles, provided convergent evidence supporting natural NNV infection. NNV RNA was detected in all ten diseased fish, whereas the other screened viral pathogens were not detected. Pooled brain-eye samples contained 4.62 × 108 to 1.33 × 109 NNV RNA copies/μg total RNA, and abundant NNV RNA was also detected in brain, spleen, kidney, and trunk tissues. Histological examination showed vacuolar and degenerative lesions in the brain and retina, and TEM revealed numerous non-enveloped, spherical virus-like particles approximately 25 nm in diameter in neural tissues, consistent with NNV morphology. Phylogenetic analysis of the RNA2 capsid protein gene placed the detected virus within the RGNNV RNA2 lineage. Together, the neurological signs, NNV RNA detection, compatible histopathological lesions, NNV-like particles in neural tissues, and RNA2 phylogenetic evidence provide evidence of natural NNV infection in T. septentrionalis. These findings document evidence of natural NNV infection in T. septentrionalis under aquaculture conditions, highlight the need for further investigations into pathogenicity and transmission, and provide a basis for VNN surveillance and biosecurity management in filefish aquaculture.

title: Clinical and Microbiological Outcomes of Topical 2% Acetic Acid as an Adjunct to Standardized Treatment for Pseudomonas aeruginosa-Associated Secondary Cutaneous Disease in Horses with Chronic Progressive Lymphedema: A Retrospective Historical-Control Cohort Study.
abstract: Chronic progressive lymphedema (CPL) in draft horses is frequently complicated by secondary cutaneous infection, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa may be difficult to eliminate. This study evaluated topical 2% acetic acid as an adjunct to a standardized local treatment protocol. Records of 35 hospitalized horses with CPL in which P. aeruginosa was the sole pretreatment isolate were reviewed retrospectively. Seven historical controls received clipping, chlorhexidine cleansing, drying, and polyhexanide irrigation; 28 horses received the same protocol plus 2% acetic acid twice daily. No horse received systemic antimicrobials. Follow-up cultures were collected 24 h after clinical resolution. Median treatment duration was 12 days (IQR 11-14) in controls and 8 days (IQR 7-9) with acetic acid (p < 0.001). P. aeruginosa clearance was achieved in 1/7 (14.3%) and 27/28 (96.4%) horses, respectively (p < 0.001). Subsequent clinical reappearance of P. aeruginosa-associated disease occurred in 6/7 (85.7%) and 3/28 (10.7%) horses (p < 0.001); most control events reflected persistence rather than recurrence after clearance. No local adverse reactions were recorded. Adding topical 2% acetic acid was associated with higher P. aeruginosa clearance, shorter treatment, and fewer subsequent clinical reappearances. Prospective randomized studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: A Horse Facial Individual Recognition Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv11n.
abstract: Rapid and accurate horse identity identification is an important prerequisite for the digital and intelligent management of livestock breeding. Traditional horse identification methods struggle to balance inference speed and recognition accuracy. In view of this, this paper takes a self-built dataset as the research object and proposes a horse identity detection algorithm based on YOLOv11n. The algorithm mainly makes three improvements: first, the traditional Conv layer is replaced by the Adaptive Kernel Convolution (AKConv) layer to enhance the adaptability of the model to targets of different sizes; second, an improved bi-level routing attention mechanism (BiFormer) is introduced into the C2PSA module to form the C2PSA-BiFormer module, which can efficiently capture long-range dependencies and effectively improve the performance of the model; finally, based on the idea of the Inner-IoU auxiliary box, the CIoU loss function is improved to further enhance the detection accuracy of the model. The experimental results show that, compared with the original model, the precision, recall, and mAP are increased by 7.5, 9.4, and 3.1 percentage points, respectively. The algorithm can effectively realize rapid horse identification and provides a methodological reference for the digitalization and intelligence of livestock breeding, showing high application value.

title: Bacteriophages Infecting Escherichia coli from Equine Production Environments in Córdoba, Colombia: Isolation, Host Range and Stability.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance has renewed interest in bacteriophages as biological control agents. Here we characterized bacteriophages infecting Escherichia coli from equine production environments in Córdoba, Colombia. Four phages were isolated by enrichment on E. coli ATCC 11229, with titers of 108-109 PFU/mL and DNA genomes, confirmed by differential DNase and RNase digestion. Phage M2, selected for biological characterization, was stable at 4 °C for 15 days and at pH 7.5 for 8 h, but lost more than 4 log10 at 30 and 45 °C and more than 3 log10 at pH ≤ 6.0 within the first hour. Of nine strains tested, M2 lysed only the isolation host and Salmonella enterica serovar Enteritidis ATCC 13076, indicating a narrow host range with intergeneric activity. M2 lysed the host culture within 35-40 min at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 2.4 × 10-1, as effectively as at MOI 2.4, and at all MOIs down to 2.4 × 10-7 (virulence index Vp = 0.85). Final titers remained at 108-109 PFU/mL despite inocula spanning seven orders of magnitude, confirming productive replication. This is the first isolation of E. coli bacteriophages from equine production environments in Colombia and the first assessment of their stability under tropical conditions.

title: Ovine Papillomavirus Type 1 DNA Positivity Is Associated with Distinct Uterine Microbial Communities in Mares During Estrus.
abstract: Uterine flushings were collected from 45 apparently healthy mares during estrus from eight stud farms in Italy: one in Campania, five in Basilicata, and two in Calabria. Samples were analyzed using digital polymerase chain reaction (dPCR) and 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. OaPV1 DNA was the only genotype detected by dPCR and was identified in 17 samples, while 28 samples were negative. Sequencing of 16S rRNA characterized and compared uterine microbiota and predicted metabolic pathways between OaPV1-positive and OaPV1-negative mares. Six major phyla were identified: Firmicutes, Proteobacteria, Actinobacteriota, Bacteroidota, Fusobacteriota, and Synergistota. Although OaPV1-positive samples showed no significant differences in microbial richness, they exhibited significant alterations in community evenness and overall microbial structure across all tested metrics, with weighted UniFrac explaining the largest proportion of variance (R2 = 0.134). Differential abundance analysis identified 43 taxa across six phyla that differed between groups, including enrichment of potentially pathogenic genera (Murdochiella, Clostridia_UCG-014, and Cellulomonas) and depletion of potentially beneficial groups (Clostridia_vadinBB60_group and Taylorella). Functional prediction revealed 108 differentially represented KEGG pathways, mainly related to amino acid biosynthesis, carbohydrate and energy metabolism, and the TCA cycle. These findings suggest an association between OaPV1 status and uterine microbiota alterations. Further studies are warranted to investigate the potential bidirectional interplay between papillomavirus infection and reproductive tract dysbiosis.

title: First Detection of γH2AX in Equine Spermatozoa Through Flow Cytometry and Its Association with DNA Status and Apoptotic-like Changes.
abstract: Histone H2A family member X phosphorylated at serine 139 (γH2AX) is a marker of the cellular response to DNA double-strand breaks. To our knowledge, this study reports the detection of γH2AX by flow cytometry in equine spermatozoa and provides preliminary evidence through its association with DNA status n and apoptotic-like changes. A total of 64 semen samples from 12 stallions were analyzed under routine field conditions. Sperm viability, mitochondrial membrane potential, Annexin V positivity, and γH2AX levels were assessed using multiparametric flow cytometry. γH2AX showed a wide distribution among samples and was correlated with Annexin V positivity and PI positivity. Linear mixed-effects models, including stallion as a random effect, identified significant associations between γH2AX levels and both Annexin V positivity and PI positivity. In contrast, γH2AX was not significantly related to sperm viability or mitochondrial membrane potential. These findings indicate that γH2AX-associated fluorescence can be detected in equine spermatozoa and is associated with indicators of apoptotic-like changes and DNA instability, which may be related to nuclear DNA damage rather than general sperm functional status. The observed associations suggest that γH2AX may have potential as an additional parameter in multiparametric flow cytometry approaches for the assessment of sperm nuclear status in stallions. However, further validation against established DNA damage assays and appropriate specificity controls is required to determine whether γH2AX fluorescence provides a specific measure of sperm nuclear DNA damage.

title: Resilient to the Thermal Challenge: Limited Effects of Climate Change on the Potential Global Distribution of the Horse Fly Atylotus agrestis (Diptera: Tabanidae).
abstract: Atylotus agrestis (Wiedemann) is a widespread Afrotropical-Palearctic horse fly and an efficient mechanical vector of livestock trypanosomes. However, its climatic limits and potential responses to climate change remain poorly understood. We modelled its potential global distribution using MaxEnt, based on 87 spatially thinned occurrence records and four weakly correlated bioclimatic predictors (BIO1, BIO4, BIO12 and BIO15). We then projected the model onto future climate scenarios for 2050 and 2070 under RCP 2.6 and RCP 8.5, using a single climate model (MRI-CGCM3). Model performance was good (AUC = 0.89; TSS = 0.64) based on presence-background cross-validation. Temperature seasonality was the most influential predictor, while suitability increased with annual mean temperature and peaked at intermediate levels of temperature and precipitation seasonality. Climatic suitability was concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa, peninsular India and South-East Asia. The model also predicted suitable conditions in Australia, where the species has not been recorded; this prediction represents an unvalidated extrapolation beyond the calibration area rather than a confirmed part of the species' potential range. Future projections largely preserved this geographic pattern, with net changes in suitable area ranging from +1.9% (2050, RCP 2.6) to -3.5% (2070, RCP 8.5). Localised losses were projected along the southern margin of the Sahara, with no poleward expansion into central or northern Europe. Climatic novelty was concentrated mainly in the Sahara and Arabian Peninsula. Overall, A. agrestis faces changing thermal conditions but appears climatically resilient under the climate model and scenarios examined. Its veterinary importance is therefore more likely to persist than to expand or decline substantially, although climatic suitability should not be interpreted as a measure of species occupancy or disease risk.

title: Biogeographic Reorganization of Horse-Associated Tabanidae Assemblages in the Neotropical Region: Species Turnover, Numerical Concentration, and Seasonality.
abstract: Horse flies (Diptera: Tabanidae) are hematophagous insects of veterinary importance, but how horse-associated assemblages are reorganized across Neotropical biogeographic units remains poorly integrated. We compared 11 validated study-level assemblages to test whether richness comparisons were sensitive to unequal sample size and sampling heterogeneity (H1) and whether biogeographic differentiation was driven mainly by species replacement rather than nestedness (H2). Observed richness was not significantly associated with validated capture size or reported campaigns, but individual-based rarefaction substantially changed richness rankings. Multiple-site Sørensen beta diversity was strongly attributable to Simpson turnover in the core (94.5%) and sensitivity (94.6%) datasets, and mean turnover increased descriptively across progressively deeper Morrone biogeographic separation classes. Across seven quantitative core assemblages, median Top1, Top3, and Top5 contributions were 49.2%, 68.4%, and 81.0%, respectively, and six species occupied the Top1 position. Annual Top1 taxa retained dominance in only 50-75% of positive sampling periods in four temporally resolved studies. Thus, horse-associated assemblages differ primarily through species replacement, while most abundance is concentrated in a small, geographically and temporally variable subset of taxa. Locally and seasonally abundant species are rational first-pass targets for pathogen screening and behavioral investigation, but abundance does not imply vector competence or transmission risk.

title: Environmental ESKAPE Organisms and Other Environmental Equine-Specific Indicator Pathogens-Are They Relevant in Equine Nosocomial Wound Infections?
abstract: Background: Multidrug-resistant organisms increasingly challenge infection prevention and control (IPC) in equine referral hospitals. Objectives: Assessment of selected environmental indicator pathogens in an equine teaching hospital and evaluation of their relevance for nosocomial wound infections. Study design: Observational study with repeated environmental sampling and retrospective evaluation of wound culture submissions. Methods: During three sampling periods (SPs), surface samples were collected across functional areas before and after routine cleaning/disinfection. Revision of the cleaning/disinfection protocols and environmental support staff feedback and training was performed between SP 1 and 2. Indicator pathogens were defined as an equine-adapted ESKAPEE-derived panel. Samples from surgical wounds were considered nosocomial if infection developed ≥3 days after hospitalisation. Results: Indicator pathogens were detected in all SPs, with the greatest frequency and diversity in SP 1. SP 1 yielded indicator pathogens in 25.7% of the 152 samples. After IPC optimisation, detection decreased in SP 2 to 11.2% of the 152 samples. In SP 3 with fewer samples (n = 42) sporadic recovery (7.1%) was observed. Contamination involved in particular high-touch surfaces and floors, and several pathogens persisted after cleaning/disinfection. Of 125 wounds, 38 met the criteria for nosocomial infection. Isolated from both, the environment and infected wounds were Streptococcus equi ssp. zooepidemicus, Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Enterobacter cloacae. Molecular typing was unavailable. Conclusions: Environmental equine-relevant indicator pathogens were detected across clinical areas. Some persisted after routine cleaning and/or were detected in nosocomial wound infections. Revision of cleaning/disinfection protocols with staff training was temporarily associated with reduced environmental contamination.

title: Equine-Assisted Physiotherapy Based on Neuroproprioceptive "Facilitation and Inhibition" Principles Combined with Gene Therapy in a 4-Year-Old Girl with Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type II: A Case Report on Functional, Respiratory, Neuromuscular, Quality-of-Life, and Molecular Outcomes.
abstract: Objectives: To describe longitudinal changes in functional performance, movement quality, respiratory function, and exploratory biological changes during intensive rehabilitation based on neuroproprioceptive "facilitation and inhibition" principles in a child with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). Methods: This case report describes a girl with SMA type II receiving disease-modifying therapy, including gene therapy, who completed three intensive rehabilitation programs based on neuroproprioceptive "facilitation and inhibition" principles, alternating equine-assisted and individualized outpatient physiotherapy. Clinical, biomechanical, respiratory, and functional outcomes were assessed before and after each therapeutic block. Exploratory molecular analyses were performed only during the second and third programs. International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF)-based documentation and home video recordings were obtained before each rehabilitation program and 28 days after completion. Results: Following rehabilitation, improvements were observed in cervical muscle endurance, gross motor function, upper-limb movement quality, spontaneous motor activity, and functional independence. After two rehabilitation blocks, the child successfully performed expiratory maneuvers yielding numerical spirometric results, although the absence of baseline values precluded quantification of changes in respiratory function. The Expanded Hammersmith Functional Motor Scale score increased from 48 to 54 points. The primary outcome, the standard Children's Hospital of Philadelphia Infant Test of Neuromuscular Disorders (CHOP INTEND) score, remained at its maximum of 64/64 throughout. This persistent ceiling effect precluded detection of further changes using the standard score. Three-dimensional motion analysis documented changes consistent with movement goals defined from the pre-intervention clinical assessment, particularly after Equine-Assisted Physiotherapy based on Neuroproprioceptive "Facilitation and Inhibition" (NEUROEQUIP-SMA). Exploratory analysis of peripheral blood long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) expression showed variable temporal changes across the rehabilitation periods, the biological significance of which cannot be determined from a single participant. Conclusions: This case illustrates continued motor development and changes in movement quality during intensive rehabilitation following gene therapy in a child with SMA type II. The contribution of physiotherapy cannot be separated from ongoing development and pharmacological treatment effects and warrants further investigation.

title: Sensitivity and Prognostic Value of DNA Damage Assays in Stallion Spermatozoa.
abstract: Environmental and biochemical factors can compromise the DNA integrity of equine spermatozoa. Several sperm DNA damage assays exist, but their relative prognostic value has not been assessed in the horse. This study compared four assays for detecting DNA damage in stallion spermatozoa: the sperm chromatin structure assay (SCSA), the sperm chromatin dispersion assay (SCD), the single-cell gel electrophoresis (comet) assay, and the 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) ELISA. Experiment 1 assessed the effect of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), a driver of oxidative stress, on sperm DNA damage across increasing concentrations and incubation times. Experiment 2 assessed arachidonic acid (AA), an upstream driver of endogenous oxidative stress. Experiment 3 evaluated the prognostic value of each assay using semen from Thoroughbred stallions during periods of high and low fertility. Across experiments, the comet assay detected DNA damage at lower stressor doses and shorter incubation times than the other assays and was the only assay to distinguish semen from low-fertility stallions from that of high-fertility stallions. The SCSA, SCD, and 8-OHdG ELISA were comparatively less sensitive in detecting significant differences under the same conditions. In conclusion, the comet assay demonstrated the most consistent responsiveness in detecting sperm DNA damage in stallions under the tested conditions.

title: Stable Production and Functional Characterization of Recombinant Eel Follicle-Stimulating Hormone Analog Incorporating an eCG β-Subunit CTP and a Flexible GGSA Linker in CHO DG44 Cells.
abstract: This study aimed to develop bioactive single-chain recombinant eel follicle-stimulating hormone (rec-eel FSH) analogs in Chinese hamster ovary DG44 (CHO DG44) cells. Our previous studies demonstrated that the O-linked glycosylated carboxyl-terminal peptide (CTP) of the equine chorionic gonadotropin (eCG) β-subunit enhances secretion in mammalian cells. Based on this observation, an FSH mutant (FSH-eM) was generated by inserting the eCG β-subunit CTP (amino acids 115-149) between the β- and α-subunits of wild-type single-chain eel FSH. Strep- and His-tags were fused to the C-terminus of the α-subunit for protein purification. The recombinant FSH-eM-Strep and FSH-eM-His proteins migrated as broad bands at 48-53 kDa. Sequential enzymatic digestion with PNGase F, O-glycosidase, and neuraminidase revealed the presence of both N- and O-linked glycans. To further investigate the potential of this approach as a candidate glycoengineering strategy, a flexible 15-amino acid linker [(GGSA)3GGG] was inserted between the β-subunit and the eCG β-subunit CTP, generating the FSH-GGSA-eM-Strep construct. Recombinant FSH-GGSA-eM-Strep was stably expressed in CHO DG44 cells and purified by Strep-Tactin XT affinity chromatography, demonstrating its suitability for large-scale production. Western blotting and silver staining showed an apparent molecular weight of 52-56 kDa. Following treatment with PNGase F, O-glycosidase, and neuraminidase, the molecular weight decreased to approximately 38, 42, and 42 kDa, respectively. cAMP accumulation assays demonstrated that rec-FSH-GGSA-eM-Strep stimulated eel FSHR-expressing cells in a dose-dependent manner. ERK1/2 phosphorylation reached a maximum at 5 min and rapidly declined thereafter. This response was markedly attenuated by treatment with the protein kinase A (PKA) inhibitor H89, suggesting that PKA activity contributes to ERK1/2 activation under the conditions tested. These findings suggest that this strategy may represent a promising approach for the production of biologically active recombinant eel FSH, with potential applications in reproductive biotechnology.

title: Genome-Wide Analysis in Equine Genomics: Population Genomics, Genetic Variation, and Functional Traits.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Genomic technologies have significantly expanded the possibilities for studying the genetic structure, diversity, and functional traits of domestic horses (Equus caballus). This review provides a critical synthesis of current advances in whole-genome analysis of horses, including the development of the EquCab2.0 and EquCab3.0 reference genomes, SNP arrays, whole-genome sequencing (WGS), long-read sequencing, and functional genome annotation. The review examines current understanding of genetic diversity and population structure in horse breeds, demographic history, genetic differentiation, introgression, and genomic inbreeding. Particular attention is paid to the analysis of runs of homozygosity (ROHs) and effective population size (Ne), as well as their significance for monitoring genetic erosion and the conservation of local and endangered breeds. The results of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and other approaches used to study morphological traits, athletic performance and endurance, coat color, reproductive characteristics, adaptation, and hereditary diseases are summarized. It is shown that the genetic architecture of traits varies significantly: from relatively large effects of individual loci to complex polygenic control, in which the influence of individual variants is limited. Therefore, statistical associations require functional validation and integration with transcriptomic, epigenomic, and other multi-omics data. The future of the field lies in expanding WGS resources, implementing pangenomic approaches, including understudied breeds, integrating modern and ancient genomes, improving genomic selection, and increasing the accuracy of genomic prediction. Such an integrated approach can improve our understanding of the genetic basis of complex traits, enhance the effectiveness of breeding programs, and simultaneously support the conservation of genetic diversity in horses.

title: Maternal Obesity and Insulin Dysregulation in Horses: Evidence and Research Priorities for Heavy Draft Mares.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Direct evidence linking maternal obesity or insulin dysregulation to reproductive and foal outcomes in heavy draft mares remains sparse. We used supplementary searches in Web of Science and Scopus to identify original equine studies for this narrative review. We assessed their applicability to heavy draft mares and considered pre-existing adiposity, excess energy intake, ration composition and insulin status separately. Low prebreeding body condition was associated with poorer reproductive performance. The association between obesity and conception remains uncertain. In a cohort of light-breed mares, maternal obesity was associated with lower offspring insulin sensitivity at 6 and 18 months and more frequent osteochondrosis at 12 months. Follow-up analyses found differences in colostrum fatty acid profiles and a lower proportion of capric acid in milk at day 90. Selected placental measures at term showed no clear group differences. After transfer, a smaller proportion of embryos from overfed Shetland pony donors survived to gestational day 28. In an energy- and protein-matched supplement comparison, foals of mares fed the higher-starch supplement had higher baseline glucose concentrations through 80 days of age, within the normal range. Prospective studies should assess maternal exposures separately and track reproductive, lactation and foal outcomes in heavy draft mares.

title: Current Understanding of the Role of MMPs and TIMPs in Veterinary Medicine: Review of the Literature Focusing on the Horse.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are zinc-dependent endopeptidases involved in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Their activity is regulated by tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs), maintaining a dynamic balance between matrix degradation and synthesis. Dysregulation of this system can contribute to pathological tissue alterations and various diseases. This review summarizes the current literature on the role of MMPs and TIMPs in diseases affecting various organ systems in veterinary medicine, with a particular focus on the horse and selected conditions in other species. Diseases of the musculoskeletal system, respiratory tract, ocular, gastrointestinal, reproductive, and cardiovascular systems, as well as the central nervous system, neoplastic and infectious diseases are discussed. MMP-2 and MMP-9 in particular are associated with inflammatory and degenerative processes. Increased activity of these gelatinases has been reported in osteoarthritis, laminitis, equine asthma, corneal ulceration, chronic enteropathies, neoplastic diseases and fibrotic disorders. Alterations in the MMP/TIMP balance further indicate pathologic tissue remodeling, angiogenesis, tumor invasion and fibrosis. Individual MMPs may serve as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. However, differences between species, organs and disease stages highlight the need for standardized investigations to clarify their pathophysiological significance and clinical utility in veterinary medicine.

title: From Observation to Welfare Inference in the Domestic Horse: Biological Context, Converging Evidence and Temporal Trajectories.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Equine welfare assessment requires interpretation of behavioural, clinical, physiological and contextual data to infer welfare-relevant mental experiences. Contemporary welfare frameworks already organise conditions relevant to both negative and positive welfare. Recent care frameworks distinguish care and management practices from their intended effects on the animal's affective state. They also place greater emphasis on meaningful choice and agency. This structured critical narrative review proposes the Equine Welfare Inference Framework (EWIF) as a complementary reasoning framework for a narrower problem: how to make the evidential pathway and the confidence in a welfare interpretation explicit when findings are incomplete, partly redundant, discordant or time-dependent. EWIF does not claim novelty for the individual principles of considering alternatives, multiple indicators, context or longitudinal change; its proposed contribution is their explicit integration around the sequence from finding to biological process, candidate internal state, welfare interpretation and confidence. Exploratory searches were followed by 34 predefined PubMed searches, yielding 6098 search-result occurrences and 4071 unique records after deduplication. Sensitivity-preserving screening retained 2274 records as a broad evidence reservoir for source discovery and conceptual coverage; these records were not a conventional set of studies, were not all independently assessed in full text, and did not contribute equally to the framework. Central claims underwent targeted source-level checks, with coverage and access limitations considered in the interpretation of the evidence. EWIF applies symmetrically to proposed positive and negative states: it asks whether additional findings provide genuinely independent support, whether disagreement reflects timing or different biological processes, and how responses change and resolve over time. It can be applied across ridden and driven exercise, handling, veterinary procedures, transport, routine management and breeding without replacing context-specific instruments. EWIF is a conceptual framework that requires empirical testing for reproducibility and practical value.

title: Effect of Storage Conditions on Equine Herpesvirus-1 DNA Detection in Equine Urine.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Equine herpesvirus-1 (EHV-1) is a major equine pathogen causing myeloencephalopathy, abortion, and respiratory disease. Following the detection of EHV-1 DNA in urine from naturally infected horses, urine has emerged as a potential complementary non-invasive specimen for molecular diagnosis. However, the influence of storage conditions on EHV-1 DNA stability remains unknown. Urine from six healthy horses was experimentally inoculated with EHV-1 (104 copies/µL) and stored at room temperature (25 °C) or under refrigeration (4 °C), with or without a commercial urine preservative, or at -80 °C without preservative. Viral DNA was quantified by qPCR over 30 days, and viral infectivity was explored by cell culture. Detectable EHV-1 DNA declined significantly during the first 24 h at room temperature and under refrigeration and remained relatively stable thereafter. Refrigeration partially improved the preservation of detectable viral DNA, whereas storage at -80 °C provided the greatest stability among the conditions evaluated over the 30-day study period. The commercial preservative provided no consistent benefit. These findings provide preliminary evidence to inform storage practices for equine urine samples intended for EHV-1 molecular diagnosis. Further studies involving naturally infected horses and additional freezing temperatures are needed to establish definitive recommendations for clinical sample handling.

title: Comparison of owners' perceptions and observed welfare conditions in stables for cold-blooded and warm-blooded horses.
abstract: Animal welfare assessment requires the integration of objective welfare indicators with owners' perceptions to identify potential gaps between management practices and actual welfare outcomes. This study evaluated welfare conditions in stables for cold-blooded and warm-blooded horses in Slovenia by comparing owners' self-assessed importance of welfare parameters with structured observational assessments conducted by veterinarians. Welfare was assessed across five welfare parameters: general status, animal behaviour, health status, living conditions and environmental conditions, using a harmonised owners' questionnaire and welfare assessment protocol. Statistically significant discrepancies were found between owners' perceptions and observed conditions across all welfare parameters, with the largest gaps identified in environmental and living conditions, particularly regarding dust levels, ammonia odour and thermal comfort within horse stables. Owners generally rated welfare parameters more positively than was supported by observational findings. Participation in professional education and training was associated with improved welfare outcomes and more accurate owner perceptions, whereas years of experience alone did not show a meaningful association with observed welfare conditions. Differences between cold-blooded and warm-blooded horse stables were most pronounced in environmental conditions, reflecting variations in housing systems and management practices. These findings indicate that owner perception alone is insufficient for reliable welfare evaluation and highlight the importance of structured welfare assessments and targeted educational interventions to improve equine welfare, particularly regarding stable environments.

title: Five-year spatio-temporal occurrence of Culicoides biting midges and arbovirus surveillance at livestock-associated sites in the Republic of Korea, 2021-2025.
abstract: Culicoides biting midges are hematophagous vectors of arboviruses in livestock, and characterizing their occurrence patterns is fundamental to disease surveillance. Field collections show substantial year-to-year variation, complicating characterization of dominant-species occurrence from a single season or site. This study integrated five years of Culicoides collection data from livestock-associated sites in the Republic of Korea to describe species composition, year-to-year variation, site-level dominance, and seasonal occurrence patterns of dominant species, while screening collected Culicoides for selected arboviruses of veterinary importance. Culicoides spp. were collected biweekly from May to October during 2021-2025 at nine livestock-associated sites (seven cattle sheds and two racetracks) using ultraviolet blacklight traps. Specimens were identified morphologically, with molecular confirmation by COI sequencing when required. All pooled samples were screened by RT-PCR for bluetongue virus (BTV), African horse sickness virus (AHSV), and Simbu serogroup viruses. Descriptive summaries of species composition, year-to-year variation, site-level dominance, and seasonal occurrence were complemented by PERMANOVA and NMDS based on Bray-Curtis dissimilarities as supplementary analyses. A total of 41,259 individuals were collected from 476 collection events, of which 277 were positive, and 199 yielded no Culicoides. The community was strongly dominated by three species (C. arakawae, C. punctatus, and C. oxystoma), which together accounted for 95.1% of all individuals. Mean abundance per collection event was the highest in 2021 and 2022 and substantially lower during 2023-2025, while dominant species composition varied among years. Most sites were dominated by either C. arakawae or C. punctatus, and mean seasonal abundance peaked in June for C. punctatus, August for C. arakawae, and September for C. oxystoma. Site effects on community composition exceeded year effects, and none of the 766 Culicoides pools screened tested positive for BTV, AHSV, or Simbu serogroup viral RNA. Although this dataset does not constitute a spatially balanced nationwide survey, integrating multi-year livestock-associated collection data provides a descriptive baseline for the spatio-temporal occurrence of dominant Culicoides species and arbovirus screening in the Republic of Korea, supporting future vector surveillance and risk assessment.

title: Equine mesenchymal stromal cells dual-primed with TGF-β1 and IL-1β or TNF-α improve epithelial healing in vitro.
abstract: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) secrete paracrine factors that contribute to their ability to promote tissue healing and regeneration. Priming equine MSCs with cytokines like TGF-β is known to enhance expression of growth factors and extracellular matrix molecules, which may increase their potential for treating certain injuries including epithelial wounds. We hypothesized that dual priming equine MSCs with TGF-β1 plus the inflammatory cytokines IL-1β or TNF-α would further increase expression of paracrine factors relevant to epithelial healing and their therapeutic potential. We also compared paracrine factor expression from primed equine MSCs with primed human induced MSCs to understand if the results in equine cells may be directly translatable to human regenerative medicine. Priming equine MSCs did not affect the morphology or viability of the cells. Equine MSCs dual-primed with TGF-β1 + IL-1β or TGF-β1 + TNF-α had increased production of PGE2 and increased expression of AREG, and HBEGF. Conditioned media from both naïve and primed MSCs increased wound closure rates in an epithelial cell migration assay and dual-primed MSCs significantly increased the proliferation colonoids in a co-culture model. Priming human induced MSCs did not stimulate the same changes in paracrine factor expression seen in equine MSCs. Priming equine MSCs with TGF-β1 + IL-1β or TGF-β1 + TNF-α is a promising strategy for generating cells or conditioned media with the necessary growth factors and cytokines to promote epithelial healing.

title: Ebola virus-based antibody products cross-neutralize 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein.
abstract: The ongoing 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease has highlighted the urgent need for therapeutic countermeasures. Whether Ebola virus (EBOV)-induced antibodies can cross-neutralize contemporary BDBVs is unclear. Here we test a diverse panel of EBOV-derived polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies, including plasma from humans after EBOV infection and horse plasma and mice serum immunized with available EBOV immunogens, against vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudotypes presenting BDBV-2026 glycoprotein (GP). We find that all antibodies retain cross-neutralizing activity against BDBV-2026 glycoprotein. These findings identify existing Ebola virus-derived antibody preparations as candidates for rapid evaluation.

title: Cone Beam Computed Tomography in Veterinary Medicine: Comparison to Conventional Cross-Sectional Imaging and a Look at Current Applications.
journal: The Veterinary clinics of North America. Small animal practice
abstract: Cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) is becoming more widely available and used in veterinary medicine. It offers major advantages in veterinary dentistry for small animals, equids, and special species such as rabbits; complementing and sometimes replacing the need for intraoral radiography, which can be time-consuming and difficult to achieve. CBCT offers the advantage of improved spatial resolution for mineralized structures over a small field of view when compared to conventional multidetector computed tomography scans. CBCT is highly susceptible to patient motion artifacts prevalent in veterinary patients and is poor at soft tissue evaluation.

title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals the population structure and molecular epidemiology of Salmonella enterica serovar Abortusequi in Japan.
abstract: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Abortusequi (S. Abortusequi) causes equine paratyphoid, a notifiable disease that remains endemic in eastern Hokkaido, Japan. Because conventional molecular typing methods show limited discriminatory power for Japanese S. Abortusequi isolates, we evaluated the utility of whole-genome sequencing and single-nucleotide variant (SNV)-based phylogenetic analysis for molecular epidemiological investigations. The complete genome sequence of a Japanese isolate was determined and used as the reference genome for SNV analysis of 23 additional isolates together with eight publicly available genomes. The complete genome consisted of a 4.74-Mb chromosome and a 93.8-kb virulence plasmid closely related to pSLT of S. enterica serovar Typhimurium LT2. SNV-based phylogenetic analysis revealed two major clades, with Japanese isolates forming a distinct lineage separated from non-Japanese isolates. Pairwise SNV distances among Japanese isolates were no greater than 60 despite spanning approximately 30 years, indicating the long-term persistence of genetically conserved endemic lineages. Two subclades identified within the Japanese lineage were also supported by network analysis. The Simpson's index of diversity of SNV-based typing was 0.94, compared with 0.10 for pulsed-field gel electrophoresis and fluorescent amplified fragment length polymorphism analysis. These findings demonstrate that whole-genome SNV analysis provides a highly discriminatory tool for molecular epidemiological investigation of endemic S. Abortusequi strains in Japan.

title: Lipidomic profiling of endometrial tissue and plasma from mares with normal and fibrotic endometrium†.
abstract: Endometrial fibrosis is a major cause of infertility in mares. It is associated with tissue remodeling and malfunction, but despite extensive research, the pathogenesis remains incompletely understood and the role of lipids in inflammation and fibrosis in the equine endometrium is largely unknown. Endometrial biopsies and blood plasma were collected from mares during diestrus. Following histopathological evaluation of tissue sections, mares were assigned to three groups: normal endometrium without fibrosis (controls, n=9), moderate endometrial fibrosis (n=9), or severe endometrial fibrosis (n=9). Using high-resolution mass spectrometry, the lipidomes of endometrial tissue and plasma were analyzed, enabling the first lipidomic profiling of equine endometrial fibrosis. Identified lipids were validated by tandem mass spectrometry (<3 ppm mass error). Glycerophospholipids and sphingomyelins were detected at lower abundance in endometrial tissue and higher abundance in plasma from mares with endometrial fibrosis compared with controls. Deoxyceramides and glycerolipids were detected at higher abundance in endometrial tissue and plasma from mares with endometrial fibrosis. Phosphatidylinositols were detected at lower abundance in endometrial tissue from mares with severe endometrial fibrosis, compared with moderate endometrial fibrosis. These findings suggest increased phosphatidylcholine turnover with cleavage of arachidonic acid for prostaglandin production, accompanied by exacerbated inflammation, compromised cellular signaling, alteration in protein and the cytoskeleton, induced tissue injury, and reduced ability to restore homeostasis in the mare endometrium with severe fibrosis. This provides a foundation for identifying lipid-based biomarkers of equine endometrial fibrosis.

title: Microsatellite-based molecular characterisation of the Majuke-type horse as a differentiated lineage within the Marwari background.
abstract: The genetic relationship between the locally recognized Majuke-type horse and Marwari has not previously been evaluated using molecular markers. We assessed whether Majuke-type represents a genetically coherent lineage or bloodline within the broader Marwari background rather than an independently founded breed. We genotyped 137 horses from stud farms in Punjab and Haryana, comprising Majuke-type (n = 18), Marwari (n = 79), and Thoroughbred (n = 40), at 20 microsatellite loci. Genetic diversity, differentiation, population structure, identity-by-state (IBS) distance, recent migration, bottleneck signals, and parentage were assessed. The panel averaged 17.75 alleles per locus and yielded strict-confidence parent-pair assignments for all 67 evaluated breeding trios. Expected heterozygosity (He) was 0.721 in Majuke-type and 0.771 in Marwari; pairwise fixation index (FST) between them was 0.107 (P = 0.0001). Population-structure analyses separated Thoroughbred from the indigenous groups and showed differentiation between Majuke-type and Marwari. BayesAss supported a recent migration signal from Majuke-type into Marwari of 6.87% ± 1.45% per generation. The sampled Majuke-type horses show reproducible microsatellite differentiation from Marwari while retaining a closer relationship to Marwari than to Thoroughbred. These results support the interpretation of Majuke-type as a differentiated Marwari-associated lineage or bloodline, but do not establish independent breed origin or registration. Genome-wide SNP data and broader sampling across farms are required to test the robustness and genomic basis of this differentiation.
